summary.text: An Ijaw city-state of the eastern Niger Delta, trading through the port of Twon-Brass at the mouth of the Brass river. Shut out of the Niger trade by the Royal Niger Company, King Koko's Nembe warriors attacked the company at Akassa in 1895 and were punished by a British force.

snapshots.title: Nembe in the creeks
snapshots.text: Nembe grows as an Ijaw kingdom; tradition dates its tenth king, Ogio, to around 1639.

snapshots.title: Two towns and a port
snapshots.text: Civil war splits Nembe into Ogbolomabiri and Bassambiri. Through Twon-Brass it trades enslaved people and then, by 1856, mostly palm oil.

snapshots.title: The Akassa raid
snapshots.text: Cut off from its markets by the Royal Niger Company's monopoly, Nembe under King Koko attacks the company depot at Akassa. A British naval force burns Nembe in reprisal.

today.text: Nembe has several Amanyanabos, for Ogbolomabiri, Bassambiri, Okpoama, Odioama and Twon-Brass, in Bayelsa State.
today.title: Amanyanabo of Nembe
